title: 500-draft cap counts stripped and erased tombstones, permanently wedging save-and-resume for the vacancy
evidence:
OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
detail: The cap subquery counts ALL rows for the vacancy, including submitted (stripped) and erased (tombstoned) rows that persist until vacancy close. 500 dead rows block every new draft (silent 200); a high-traffic listing can never offer save-and-resume again.
recommended_fix: Add AND d.submitted_at IS NULL AND d.erased_at IS NULL to the count subquery so only live drafts consume the cap.

title: Per-vacancy 500-draft cap is exceedable under concurrent first-saves (check-then-insert)
evidence:
INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)
SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND d.email = lower($2)
  )
  OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
detail: Two concurrent inserts for different new emails at count 499 both evaluate the count under READ COMMITTED snapshots and both insert, exceeding 500. The draft_cap integration test pins 500 as if absolute; the bound is only approximate.
recommended_fix: Serialize the capped insert (e.g. pg_advisory_xact_lock on vacancy_id) or document the cap as an approximate abuse bound.

title: Cross-vacancy fan-out bound (3 continue emails/recipient/hour) exceedable by concurrent claims
evidence:
AND (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  ) < 3
detail: Concurrent claims for the same recipient on different vacancies update different rows (no lock contention), so both read the same pre-stamp count and both pass — the fan_out_bound test's exact 3/hour is only race-safe per draft row, not across rows.
recommended_fix: Serialize per recipient (e.g. pg_advisory_xact_lock on lower(email)) before the count, or document the bound as approximate under concurrent attack.

title: list_resumable_draft_tokens lacks the erased_at guard every other W3-touched query has
detail: Upsert and claim both guard erased_at IS NULL; this stage-2 reminder prefetch does not. It is only safe because erase_draft_by_token NULLs continue_token in the same UPDATE — any future path setting erased_at without NULLing the token emails an erased applicant (contact-after-erasure).
recommended_fix: Add AND erased_at IS NULL to the WHERE clause for parity with the other tombstone guards.

title: Migration header still describes pre-W1 lazy token minting and pre-W3 hard-delete erasure
evidence:
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request).
...
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
detail: Round-2 W1 mints continue_token at save time (most rows now carry a token) and W3 erasure is a tombstone that keeps the row as a suppression record; the schema's own header comments assert both pre-fix behaviours.
recommended_fix: Update the two comment blocks to describe mint-at-save (COALESCE keeps existing) and the tombstone/suppression-record erasure model.
